# PB-03 immutable-artifact commit work

PB-03 removes redundant immutable-artifact work without changing the namespace
snapshot format, quotas or engine transition rules. The stable five-artifact event
case drops from **38 to 9 SQL driver calls per CAS**, while still freshly reading,
authenticating and verifying all five stored artifacts on every CAS. There is no
artifact cache or external service. Broader performance acceptance remains blocked
by PB-04: history-sensitive full-state work is still present.

## Measurement before optimization

The instrumented baseline was captured before changing artifact commit behavior.
For 24 no-consumer event admissions with five installed artifacts and no settled
history, event p95 was 30.848 ms. Per CAS, artifact-address locking made ten SQL
calls and averaged 4.826 ms; repeated artifact/link writes made twenty calls and
averaged 9.682 ms. The extra validation/canonicalization stage averaged 0.522 ms.
Each CAS performed ten successful artifact verifications (five fresh reads plus
five duplicate write-path verifications) and five additional canonicalizations.

These are SQL driver API calls, not packet counts. The pinned tokio-postgres
`ToStatement` string path prepares a statement before executing it, so a call can
involve more than one wire exchange. The diagnostic deliberately does not equate
an API call with one network round trip. SQL wait durations include those driver
operations; BEGIN and connection-mutex waiting lie outside the internal stage
spans. End-to-end PB-02 latency still includes them.

## Exact optimization and authority boundary

The owner/session advisory lock, backend PID, incarnation and expected namespace
revision are checked before reuse. The transaction locks and decodes the current
namespace row, then reads the referenced artifact bytes from PostgreSQL. Protected
bytes are authenticated under their namespace/address/key context. Canonical
artifact parsing, model validation and address verification still happen on
these fresh bytes. No previously observed metadata substitutes for that read.

The existing immutable-artifact comparison rejects a changed object under a
retained address. The optimized write path compares the **entire typed artifact**
with its freshly verified predecessor; matching a caller-supplied digest alone
cannot qualify. When unchanged and no protection refresh is required, it skips
only duplicate verification/canonicalization and redundant payload/reference
writes. New or changed addresses continue through the full validation and
persistence path; invalid replacements roll back the transaction.

New catalog addresses are inserted in one ordered batch. A second ordered query
locks the union of previous and next catalog addresses. Existing namespace
references retain their catalog foreign keys; a missing lock result refuses the
transaction. Catalog locking and disposal/reference checks remain in the same
transaction as artifact links, snapshot, receipts and indexes. Insertion and
locking use explicit digest order, including multi-address installation races.

Protected unchanged payloads keep their existing authenticated ciphertext/nonce;
this does not reuse a nonce for changed content. Snapshot encryption still writes
a new revision-bound envelope. Changing the active snapshot key forces artifact
refresh during an ordinary CAS. Explicit `reencrypt_namespace` forces every
artifact through refresh even when the active key ID is unchanged, so rotation
and explicit refresh do not become a no-op. Plaintext cleanup and cross-namespace
reference predicates are retained. Protected-store performance is not qualified
by the unprotected benchmark matrix.

## Bounded diagnostics

`PostgresStorage::set_profiling(true)` enables and resets value-free process
aggregates; `profiling_snapshot()` returns them. Profiling is disabled by default.
Only the fixed `load`/`cas` operation names and fixed stage names are recorded;
namespace names, artifact addresses, SQL strings/parameters, payloads, keys and
error text are absent. Counters saturate and retain no per-operation history.

Stage wall time includes SQL and CPU within that stage. Verification and extra
canonicalization timings overlap their containing stage, so they must not be
added again. Successful verification counts refer to the fresh-read and explicit
write-validation sites, not every internal serialization performed by model
validation. The `aborted` counter means no successful COMMIT acknowledgement from
that transaction wrapper; it is diagnostic, not proof of rollback or absence of
an uncertain external effect. Automatic rollback duration is not instrumented.

Set `AQ_PB03_STORAGE_PROFILE=1` when invoking the existing PB-02 wrapper to collect
these counters. The workload, event payloads, history sizes, concurrency, retry
cap and provisional budgets remain unchanged. Default-off experiments provide
the primary end-to-end comparison; opt-in runs explain the mechanism.

## Correctness qualification

The final candidate passes 116 database-free tests, 27 PostgreSQL tests and two
administrative CLI tests, strict workspace/all-target/all-feature Clippy and
format checks. All PostgreSQL tests use a new disposable container pinned to the
same PostgreSQL 17.11 image as PB-02.

Five new PostgreSQL regressions cover:

- Unchanged commits skip duplicate writes but reject deliberately corrupted
  backing bytes, then verify again after a cold reopen. Profiling is default-off,
  bounded and contains no namespace or synthetic secret values.
- Protected unchanged payloads retain their nonce, explicit same-key refresh
  changes it, corrupted ciphertext refuses, and a changed artifact under the
  same address cannot bypass immutable-object checks.
- Eight concurrent two-artifact GC/install races preserve shared bytes,
  references and disposal records under ordered batch locking.
- An ordinary CAS with a newly active key refreshes unchanged artifacts, allowing
  new-key-only readback and refusing old-key-only readback.
- Eight mixed old/new races let two namespaces retain different existing
  artifacts while both add the other artifact and the same brand-new third
  address; both references and bytes survive without lock inversion.

Existing ownership/incarnation/CAS, late SQL failure rollback, abrupt process
loss, GC/reference races, protected tampering, key rotation/old backups, legacy
migration and plaintext-cleanup tests also pass. No engine, compiler, model,
retention policy, migration, or namespace quota was redesigned for PB-03.

## Performance and remaining boundary

Final measurements and source hashes are in `PB-03.json` and
`PB-03.results.json`. The unchanged PB-02 full profile is repeated with diagnostics
off, and the reduced profile is repeated in two fresh databases with the same
sample counts and budgets. Instrumented baseline and optimized runs are retained
separately. PB-02's immutable evidence is unchanged.

The final default-off comparison uses the same starting states and configuration
as the committed PB-02 full experiment:

| Settled roots/events | PB-02 event p95 | PB-03 event p95 | PB-03 commit p95 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 / 0 | 28.798 ms | 17.101 ms | 11.692 ms |
| 32 / 32 | 34.941 ms | 19.985 ms | 14.152 ms |
| 128 / 128 | 56.690 ms | 42.057 ms | 30.685 ms |
| 512 / 512 | 172.370 ms | 130.369 ms | 99.026 ms |

At 512 history, six-/24-ready-root dispatch-call p95 is 145.392/157.937 ms.
Pending-child event p95 is 13.272/16.933/28.616/86.806 ms at 0/8/32/128
children. The four-thread bounded-retry admission case completes 28/32 requests;
refusals remain explicit. All five quota tests preserve unchanged state, and the
finite ready-scope prefixes remain round robin.

The two final reduced experiments retain all results: one 1-history event cell
reaches 26.797 ms, while the other reduced cells pass their stated budgets.
Earlier measurements and profile-enabled runs are retained as well. Observed
wall-time improvements on this shared host are not an uncontended latency
service guarantee; the 38-to-9 driver-call reduction identifies the mechanism.

The five-artifact default-off event p95 remains above 25 ms at 128 and 512 retained
roots/events, and ready dispatch at 512 history still exceeds 100 ms. Lower fixed
cost does not remove whole-snapshot loading, decoding, index comparison and quota
serialization. Finite passing reduced cells do not establish a steady combined
operating envelope or 500-agent capacity. PB-04/PERF-01 remain release blockers.
